title: "Jupyter"

## Start and stop

| What you want | How |
|------------|------------------------|
| Start JupyterLab with the project's environment | `pixi run jupyter lab`, from the project folder |
| The browser did not open | copy the `http://localhost:8888/lab?token=...` link from the terminal |
| Stop JupyterLab | `Ctrl-C` twice, in the terminal that runs it |

See [lesson 06, section 1](../pages/06-jupyter.qmd#start-jupyterlab).

## In a notebook

| What you want | Keys or menu |
|------------|------------------------|
| Run a cell and move to the next | `Shift-Enter` |
| Save | `Ctrl-S` (macOS: `Cmd-S`) |
| Leave the cell to use the keys below / edit it again | `Esc` / `Enter` |
| New cell above / below | `A` / `B` |
| Make the cell Markdown / code | `M` / `Y` |
| Delete the cell | `D` `D` |
| Restart and run everything, top to bottom | *Kernel → Restart Kernel and Run All Cells* |
| Clear all outputs | *Edit → Clear Outputs of All Cells* |
| Use the project's Python | *Kernel → Change Kernel → Python 3 (ipykernel)* |

The single-letter keys are JupyterLab's defaults; they work when no cell is being edited.

## From the command line

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Does it run without you? Fresh kernel, top to bottom, HTML copy | `pixi run jupyter nbconvert --execute --to html NOTEBOOK.ipynb` |
| Run it and save the outputs in the notebook | `pixi run jupyter nbconvert --execute --to notebook --inplace NOTEBOOK.ipynb` |
| Clear the outputs before you commit | `pixi run jupyter nbconvert --clear-output --inplace NOTEBOOK.ipynb` |
| Render it with Quarto, with captions and alt text | `pixi run quarto render NOTEBOOK.ipynb --execute` ([lesson 07](../pages/07-quarto.qmd#notebooks-too)) |

See [sections 3 and 5](../pages/06-jupyter.qmd#does-it-run-without-you).

## The first code cell, for paths relative to the project

```{.python}
import os
from pathlib import Path

if Path.cwd().name == "notebooks":
    os.chdir("..")
```

## Warning signs

- Execution counts out of order, such as `[1] [3] [2]`: check with *Restart Kernel and Run All Cells*.
- `NameError` on a fresh kernel: the notebook used a cell you ran earlier, moved or deleted.
- A notebook file of several MB: it holds outputs. Clear them.

## Notebook, script or report?

| | Use it for |
|-|------------|
| Notebook | exploring, trying ideas |
| `scripts/` | code you reuse and can test |
| Quarto report | results you show others ([lesson 07](../pages/07-quarto.qmd)) |

## Official cheat sheets and references

Project Jupyter has no official cheat sheet. The closest official references:

- JupyterLab, *The JupyterLab Interface*: <https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/interface.html>
- JupyterLab, *Notebooks*: <https://jupyterlab.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user/notebook.html>
- nbconvert, *Using as a command line tool*: <https://nbconvert.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage.html>
- Quarto, *JupyterLab*: <https://quarto.org/docs/tools/jupyter-lab.html>
- In JupyterLab, *Settings → Settings Editor → Keyboard Shortcuts* lists every shortcut.
